nodes.question: What are the implications of preserving mangrove ecosystems in terms of carbon emissions?
nodes.answer: Preserving mangrove ecosystems can prevent the emission of around 304 Tg of CO2e each year, significantly impacting global carbon dynamics.
nodes.paragraph: 2024). In addition to being sources of detritus, mangroves also serve as habitats for macrophytes and invertebrates, which are vital food sources for mollusks, crustaceans, and fish that are ulti- mately consumed by larger marine predators. This makes mangroves a crucial foundation for coastal food webs and the C cycle (Tang et al. 2018 Globally, BCEs are believed to contain more than 30,0 teragrams (Tg) of carbon spread across around 185 million hectares. By preserv - ing these ecosystems, it is possible to avoid the emission of approximately 304 (141 466) Tg of CO2e every year (Macreadie et al. 2021). This phenomenon significantly impacts global carbon dynamics, representing roughly 10 to 15% of carbon sequestration in coastal sediments around the world (Duarte et al. 2013). Mangroves can store three to five times more carbon than terrestrial forests (Friess et al. 2019) and 13 times more than rainforests (Maulana and Auliah 2021). nodes.question: What is projected to happen to forest cover in Southeast Asia by 2100 if current deforestation rates continue?
nodes.answer: Southeast Asia is projected to lose three-quarters of its original forest cover by 2100.
nodes.paragraph: 2011; Cushman et al. 2017; Chen et al. 2024). If cur - rent rates of deforestation persist, Southeast Asia would lose three-quarter of its original forest cover by 2100 (Achard et al. 2002), with dramatic consequences for biodiver - sity, including a projected loss of between 24 and 63% of its terrestrial endemic species (Sodhi and Brook 2006). Although habitat loss affects all taxonomic groups, carnivores are particularly vul- nerable given their low fecundity, high habitat area requirements and high vulnerability to human persecution (Cardillo et al. 2004). As habitat loss and fragmentation reduce the availability of large, intact patches of suitable habitat, carnivores are frequently restricted to small, less suitable areas, often outside protected areas and embedded within human-dominated landscapes (Crooks et al. 2017; Cushman et al. 2018; Lov - eridge et al. 2022).
